errors.english: "by one's own soul"
errors.why: bdag nyid here simply glosses rang nyid as 'oneself' (svayam), not a soul.

errors.english: such as a vase or sound
errors.why: The Tibetan gives only the space example; 'vase or sound' is not in the text.

errors.english: since things like a rabbit's horns are seen to be non-existent, this line of reasoning
errors.why: The Tibetan says this reason (being unproduced), being seen in non-existents such as a hare's horn, proves the subject space non-existent; the English makes the hare's horn's non-existence the premise.

errors.english: during a debate the treatise itself is not the primary thing being accepted
errors.why: The Tibetan says that at the time of debate a treatise is not to be adopted at all, and the clause glosses the lemma 'even if a treatise has been accepted'; 'not the primary thing' weakens this.

note: Follows the commentary on svayam in the thesis definition correctly overall, but 'soul' for bdag nyid is wrong and a few clauses are misconstrued.

errors.english:
When it arises in men who wish for harm,
They feel a certain joy;
errors.why: The anger arises in oneself and it is the ill-wishers who rejoice at it, not anger arising in the ill-wishers.

fix.find:
When it arises in men who wish for harm,
They feel a certain joy;
fix.replace:
When it arises in one, those who wish one harm
Rejoice;

errors.english: Even though I was shaken, I did not let go.
errors.why: It is the harmer (anger) that was stirring which he did not let loose, not he who was shaken; the same shift recurs in the king's question ('even while you were shaken').

errors.english: I did not understand that and acted with such instability.
errors.why: The king thinks that, not understanding, he took such a man to be inconstant (misjudged him), not that he himself acted unsteadily.

errors.english: One will not practice the ultimate meaning.
errors.why: dam pa'i don here is one's true good/welfare in a moral verse, not the philosophical 'ultimate meaning'.

errors.english: But one is said to have abandoned it [note: referring to a false accusation of losing one's temper], then bad reputation arises
errors.why: The stanza says ill repute comes to one who does not abandon heart-burning anger; the note invents a false-accusation scenario.

note: Verses on anger are mostly readable, but several agent relations in the narrative and verses are confused.
A careful rendering of a difficult dream/waking passage; the unexplained Tibetan token skyes mos left in the English should be resolved or noted.

errors.english: it would result in an infinite regress (prasanga) reductio ad absurdum
errors.why: ha cang thal ba is atiprasaṅga, absurd overextension; the regress (thug pa med pa) is argued separately afterwards.

fix.find: it would result in an infinite regress (prasanga) reductio ad absurdum
fix.replace: it would entail an absurd overextension (atiprasaṅga)

errors.english: Therefore, it is intended that space itself has no distinct parts.
errors.why: The point is that the nature is not different from space itself, not that space lacks parts.

errors.english: [note: universals and numbers]
errors.why: The two are said to be qualities (guṇa) residing only in substance; a universal is not a guṇa in Vaiśeṣika, so the note misidentifies them.

note: Argument against the Vaiśeṣika properties of space is followed, but the atiprasaṅga term and the conclusion are misrendered.
Faithful rendering of the sequence of faith and the teacher's instruction.

errors.english: it is pervaded by one portion of the direction of the property of the (subject) dharmin that is to be proven
errors.why: phyogs here is pakṣa (thesis), not 'direction'; the property of the subject is pervaded by a part of the pakṣa.

fix.find: it is pervaded by one portion of the direction of the property of the (subject) dharmin that is to be proven
fix.replace: the property of the subject (dharmin) to be proven is pervaded by a part of the thesis (pakṣa)

errors.english: the presence of the reason where the predicate is present, and its absence where the predicate is absent
errors.why: Anvaya is the presence of the probandum wherever the reason is present, not the reason wherever the predicate is; the note states the converse.

errors.english: such a distinction is impossible
errors.why: The Tibetan says concomitance holds in all instances and that (all-instance presence) is impossible in a particular, not that the distinction is impossible.

errors.english: In order to understand the pervader, it is appropriate to understand the qualified itself.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the pervaded/qualified is fit to be the means of making known (gamaka) the pervader as what is to be made known; the gamya-gamaka relation is lost.

note: Logical terminology of pakṣa, anvaya and gamaka is handled unreliably, though the overall drift of the pervasion discussion survives.

errors.english: restraining my hands from loosening her sash
errors.why: It is the girl who, in the lover's fantasy, stops his hand as it loosens her girdle, not he who restrains his own hands.

errors.english: the inner fire in the limbs arises
errors.why: yan lag med (Anaṅga) is the bodiless god of love; from imagining arises the fire of Anaṅga, a name rendered as a description.

errors.english: experiencing the agony wrought by unvirtuous deeds committed through the noisy senses, one suffers
errors.why: The clause continues onto the next side (those made pitiable by cries of pain at the hands of evil-doing beings); 'noisy senses' and the closing 'one suffers' are not in the Tibetan.

errors.english: Knowing the many faults of desiring the women of others
errors.why: The side is a series of verses (including this closing śloka) that the English runs as prose paragraphs.

note: Captures the gist of the kāvya on lust, but agents in the fantasy, the Anaṅga epithet and the final clause are mishandled.
Faithful rendering of the grammatical commentary on the verses on skill in speech.

errors.english: has committed an offense requiring a formal meeting of the community
errors.why: The Tibetan specifies a concealed saṅghāvaśeṣa offence (bcabs pa), and the pupil helps him both receive the sanction quickly and be freed; 'concealed' is lost.

note: Sound rendering of the niśraya duties and the five-fold qualifications, with one Vinaya nuance lost.
Both the Sanskrit and Tibetan verses of the bilingual side are rendered faithfully.
